solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Male model uncovered rising bias

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the assembled letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to model for an artist is to sit
something uncovered is open

explanation.surface: A man posing without clothes, perhaps, amid talk of prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' signals a reversal because in a down light the letters read from the bottom upwards; 'model' is the verb, as an artist's model sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouritism shown to relatives or friends is a form of bias in appointments.

clue.text: Prompt betting on middle of course

parts.note: SP is the starting price in horse-race betting

indicators.note: middle of tells us to take only the central letters of the word course

explanation.surface: A racegoer is urged to place a bet partway round the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds at the moment a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to urge or prompt them into action.

clue.text: Authority of vacuous older academic and laureate

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so each of the three words loses its insides and keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An empty-headed elderly don and a poet laureate are held up as an authority.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person or source regarded as an infallible authority on a subject.

clue.text: Ship's crew to pillage revealing kind of bottle

indicators.note: revealing says the run of letters is exposed within the words Ship's crew to pillage

explanation.surface: Pirates set about looting, and the haul turns out to include a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle sealed with a threaded cap that twists off is described by this type name.

clue.text: Supporter's over grass — one goes to top referee

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word for supporters is turned upside down

parts.note: a bra is a supporter; the 's stands for is, joining it to over

indicators.note: goes to top says the letter for one moves up to the start of its word

parts.note: a grass is an informer, a traitor
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A backer goes over the turf while someone rises to the top of refereeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses BRAS to ARB; in TRAITOR the I moves to the front, making ITRATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbitrator settles disputes impartially, just as a referee judges between sides.

clue.text: Transported over island

parts.note: carried or transported is borne
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone is carried across the sea to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is the large island in South-East Asia shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.

clue.text: Tense, the compiler flipped, quietly spoken and profane

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: flipped means the word for the compiler is turned round

parts.note: a setter calls himself me
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
spoken rather than written is oral

explanation.surface: An irritated setter loses his cool and speaks quietly but swears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' turns ME into EM. 'Tense' looks like the definition, as the answer relates to grammatical tense, but it only supplies T.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal means worldly or secular as opposed to spiritual, which is what profane means in its older sense.

clue.text: Stabs organ over extremities, gutted

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the organ above the next piece

parts.note: the lung is a bodily organ

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of extremities

explanation.surface: A grisly picture of body parts being stabbed and disembowelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunges are sudden thrusts, as with a sword, so they are stabs.

clue.text: Incentive to fix corrosion on motor

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the corrosion after the motor

parts.note: a motor is a car
rot is decay or corrosion

explanation.surface: Someone needs a reason to repair the rust on their car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a reward dangled to encourage someone, as before a donkey.

clue.text: Stop air unevenly producing lift

indicators.note: unevenly means taking the odd-numbered letters of the words Stop air

explanation.surface: An aircraft's air supply cut off erratically, yet it still produces lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To soar is to rise high into the air, just as to lift can mean to rise.

clue.text: Suited to wit, nun's last to enter nunnery

indicators.note: to enter says these letters go inside the word for a nunnery

parts.note: a convent is a nunnery

indicators.note: last here asks for the closing letter of the word nun

parts.note: IE (id est) means that is, to wit

explanation.surface: A nun's suitability for entering the convent is being judged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convenient fits in with one's needs, so it is suited to them.

clue.text: Possibly drill bit tackles resistance

indicators.note: tackles means the word for bit grips the resistance letter inside it

parts.note: a bit is a piece
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A drill bit meets resistance as it works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill bit' reads as one tool; 'drill' belongs to the definition and 'bit' to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill through something is one way to pierce it, hence 'Possibly'.

clue.text: Brains of university lecturer catching fire? Not quite!

indicators.note: catching means the lecturer's title wraps round the word for fire

parts.note: a reader is a senior university lecturer in Britain

indicators.note: Not quite says the word for fire stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: an ingle is a fire burning in a hearth

explanation.surface: A clever academic nearly sets himself alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite!' cuts the fire word short and 'catching' holds it inside the lecturer; a reader is a British university rank just below professor, and an ingle is a hearth fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The brains behind a scheme is its organiser, the person heading a gang of troublemakers.

clue.text: Former boyfriend's reportedly more blubbery covering

parts.note: an ex is a former boyfriend; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are heard, not seen, matching how they are said

parts.note: to blubber is to weep, so more blubbery is tearier, said aloud

explanation.surface: A spurned ex is apparently fatter than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubbery' suggests fat, but here it means weepy.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer surface or shell of something is what covers it.

clue.text: Make extremely nasty advances, creating edginess initially

definitions.text: Make extremely nasty advances, creating edginess initially

indicators.note: extremely means take the two extreme letters of Make
initially means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone makes threatening moves that leave others on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Threatening behaviour that makes people nervous is exactly what this word describes.

clue.text: New chap almost sweet about purchasing Old Spice

indicators.note: about tells us the whole assembly is turned round
purchasing means the group takes in the old letter

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: almost means the word for sweet loses its last letter

parts.note: sweet in the sense of pleasant is nice

explanation.surface: A newcomer buys a bottle of a well-known men's aftershave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims NICE to NIC; O goes in after N to give NOMANNIC, and 'about' turns that round. Old Spice is an aftershave brand, but 'Old' only gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fragrant bark of a tropical tree, used as a cooking spice.

clue.text: Inconsistent sleeper wraps up too much

indicators.note: wraps up means the word for sleeper encloses the words for too much

parts.note: a sleeper is a spy planted to lie dormant
OTT, over the top, means too much

explanation.surface: Someone asleep has piled on far too many blankets.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotty can mean patchy or uneven in quality, i.e. inconsistent.

clue.text: Raised in Kiev, also, guy's former national

indicators.note: Raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man brought up in the Ukrainian capital is described.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Raised' reads the letters inside 'Kiev, also, guy's' from bottom to top; 'in' marks them as sitting inside those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Yugoslavia no longer exists, so a citizen of it is a national of a former state.

clue.text: Farmer in outbuilding pens sheep

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the phrase Farmer in outbuilding holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A farmer shuts sheep inside a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: The merino is a breed of sheep prized for its fine wool.

clue.text: Standard leader's abandoned when following the French language

indicators.note: following places the next piece after the French article

parts.note: par is a standard or norm
la is the French feminine word for the

indicators.note: leader's abandoned says the first letter of the word for when is dropped

parts.note: once can mean when, as in once you arrive

explanation.surface: A standard-bearer leaves the French behind, speaking of language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's abandoned' strips O from ONCE, leaving NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking, a manner of language or idiom.

clue.text: Call about to turn sour

indicators.note: to turn says the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness
CA (circa) means about

explanation.surface: A call goes out that something is about to go off.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic relates to vinegar, so it means sour-tasting.

clue.text: Bird stripped in publication's English fantasy

indicators.note: in puts the stripped bird inside the publication and English

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication

indicators.note: stripped means Bird loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A naked bird appears in an English magazine, the stuff of fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' takes IR from Bird; it goes after the M of MAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, something seen that is not real, a fantasy.

clue.text: Insect against being consumed by completely heartless missus?

indicators.note: being consumed by puts the word for against inside the next piece
completely heartless empties missus of all its inner letters

parts.note: anti means against

explanation.surface: An insect eaten by a cold-hearted wife, perhaps as a mate is devoured.
explanation.walkthrough: Female mantises famously eat their mates, hence the '?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is a predatory insect.

clue.text: Bond snatching a kiss for fun

indicators.note: snatching means the bond word grabs the letters inside it

parts.note: a relation is a connection, a bond

explanation.surface: James Bond steals a kiss for pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxation is leisure or recreation, i.e. fun.

clue.text: Snake trailing Queen produces unpleasant noise

indicators.note: trailing puts the snake behind the queen

parts.note: R is short for Regina, queen
an asp is a snake

explanation.surface: A snake following the monarch hisses harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a harsh grating sound, so an unpleasant noise.

clue.text: Check head of government's out of power

indicators.note: out of says the leading letter is removed from the word for power

parts.note: to reign is to hold power, and a reign is a period of power

indicators.note: head of means take the first letter of government

explanation.surface: A political check on a government that has lost power.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain, so a rein is a check or curb.

clue.text: Orator with endless boast keeping cool

indicators.note: keeping means the trimmed boast holds the cool word
endless means the word for boast loses its last letter

parts.note: to crow is to boast
ice can mean cool, as in to ice a drink

explanation.surface: A speaker who brags non-stop while staying unruffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the great Roman statesman famed as an orator.

clue.text: Genuine old gear nearly completely 'post-fashionable'

parts.note: rig is equipment or gear
in means fashionable

indicators.note: nearly says the word for completely loses its final letter

parts.note: all means completely

explanation.surface: Vintage clothes almost entirely past their fashion are the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something original is authentic, not a copy, so it is genuine.
